impact.notes: Root cause: node-image 2026.06.18 on NP-17 pinned RX-7 IRQ to CPU48 (NUMA1) while queue memory is on NUMA0 → AAAA DNS stall → payment pool exhaustion → checkout SLO → api-gateway errors. payment-provider latency is a false lead.

service_dependencies.isolation_note: Healthy siblings (pricing/inventory/token/fraud) are not on the failing payment path; errors escalate api-gateway ← checkout ← payment ← (DNS/RX/IRQ), with payment-provider as a decoy leaf.

distributed_traces.false_lead_assessment: Payment-provider CLIENT/SERVER spans show ≈17s duration on affected traces, but sibling services remain fast and only NP-17 payment pods correlate — treat external provider as a false lead; latency is consistent with pre-provider DNS/connection stall (AAAA / pool).

remediation.guidance: Treat this as an infrastructure misconfiguration incident, not a payment-provider outage. Immediately roll NP-17 back from node image 2026.06.18 to 2026.05.30 so RX-7 IRQs pin to the same NUMA node as queue memory, then confirm kernel RX-queue latency, AAAA DNS p99, checkout p99, and checkout success rate return to baseline on the Region-B · CARD · MOBILE · INR · cart>12 slice. Do not restart payment pods as the primary fix — that only masks pool pressure. After mitigation, block cross-NUMA IRQ assignments in the node-image pipeline and stage future NP-17 rollouts on 1–2 nodes with RX/DNS watch windows before full pool promotion.
